main_text.l: Ad Qvæst. LX.
De materia prima & secunda.
Materiæ primæ, quæ intellectu difficilis est, essentia est
id, quod habet rationem differentiæ, diciturque differen-
tia in specierum constitutione. Adumbratur autem for-
malis eius substantia, ut loquar cum Scaligero, notione
aptitudinis ad receptionem formarum, Exer. 359. sect. 12.
Quo idem respicit, cum dicit, materiam primam esse puram
potentiam ad formam, ut fit elementum. Et alii: Materia enti-

l.i: tas potentialis est, unde materia ens impotentia dicitur.

Doubtful readings: "Itaque[?]" (the word before "impropriè" is hard to read), "πάσχειν[?]" (Greek, the letters are uncertain), "corpus[?]" (line-broken word), and "compositio" as read. "Ad 2." sits at the line end, not in a catchword position, so it is kept in the text. Long s written as plain s in abbreviations ("sect.", "Exer."). The paragraph starting "Concl." and the "Ass." and "Prop." lines are treated as paragraphs, not headings.
